newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - June 19.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY

- China formally established its fourth centrally administered municipality, Chongqing, on Wednesday in a ceremony attended by Premier Li Peng. The move gives Chongqing the status of a provincial government.
PEOPLE'S DAILY OVERSEAS EDITION
- China has halted construction on over 80 office buildings to save 1 billion yuan in a drive to limit extravagant spending.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- The People's Bank of China publicly unveiled its index of purchasing prices for production materials, which the central bank has used internally as a tool to gauge inflation since 1987.
- China's fixed asset investment is forecast to hit 2.8 trillion yuan in 1997, up 18.5 percent from 1996.
- Vice Governor of the People's Bank of China, Chen Yuan, warns of possible financial risk in the banking sector.
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- China's planted area of cotton has increased in most provinces this year.
MARKET DAILY
- China's output of refined lead is seen at 530,000 tonnes in 1997.
CHINA BUSINESS TIMES
- Chinese Vice Premier Wu Bangguo says conditions are more favourable in 1997 for the reform of state enterprises.
- Bank savings in Beijing have slowed due to interest rate cuts and rising investment in the stock market.
CHINA NEWS SERVICE
- Guangxi province has handed down tough sentences to 120 drug traffickers, four of whom were given the death penalty.
CHINA DAILY

- The Export & Import Bank of China has been providing long-term, low-interest loans to developing countries, which offer a way for domestic Chinese enterprises to boost exports and expand overseas economic cooperation.
